claim: The E1 entry is precisely localized: both images walk an identical wandering path through the .CODE/.DATA region, and at step 6483 the working mbir_cmp_lt.mb executes IN (reads the first stdin byte) while mbir_cmp_lt_dec.mb executes HALT one step later. The program never reads stdin, which is why the class flags are constant and the output is input-independent.
claim_status: ASSEMBLED, ENTRY MISROUTED (localized to one instruction)

decisive_trace_comparison.method: instrumented trace of c, d, a per instruction, 20,000 steps, stdin '1 2'

working_image.first_IN_note: a <- 49 ('1'), i.e. the first stdin byte

e1_image.note: no IN instruction is ever executed; it HALTs one step after where the working image reads

decisive_trace_comparison.reading: the two images share the same wandering path through the flag/cell region (identical for the first 200 steps and beyond), and the path terminates at my HALT cell instead of at an entry that reads stdin

root_cause: The program's entry is not wired: the position-dependent opcode decode (op = (cell + c) % 94, so the SAME cell decodes differently at different addresses) routes the wandering path to my HALT cell. My .CODE layout was written from scratch and does not place the code blocks where the wandering path lands.

fix_required.primary: Do not write the .CODE layout from scratch. Take the WORKING image vmir_cmp_lt.hell as the base: keep its .CODE/.DATA layout and its entry wiring verbatim (same repository, MIT), and change only the comparison logic. Its wandering path already lands on its ENTRY.
fix_required.secondary: If the layout must stay custom, make the leading .CODE cell sequence match a working image's exactly, and place the ENTRY block at the address the wandering path reaches.

verification.reading: both symptoms follow from the single root cause: no stdin is ever read, so the classification cannot vary, and the emitted bytes are whatever the wandering path leaves in the accumulator

what_is_demonstrated: The image assembles at 21,487 bytes with 37,562 bytes of headroom.
The transplanted decrement_value removed the infinite loop.
The entry failure is localized to one instruction: step 6484 HALT versus step 6483 IN in the working image.
what_remains: Rewire the entry (preferably by basing the program on mbir_cmp_lt.hell's working layout).
Then wire the digit reader to the class flags, resolve the engine disagreement, and re-run the grid.
scope_limits: No code from the GPL-3 example_adder.hell; all reused code is this repository's own MIT.
